answer: One way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is to tie each agent identity to costly, slow-to-build reputation instead of a free key. A new agent starts with no history, and its early work is checked by peers who already have standing. Every verified action joins a thread of signed records, so faking a thousand agents means building a thousand long histories by hand. Rewards are held back like cargo at a wharf until inspection clears them. Locked stake acts like a marble in a pocket: cheap to hold, expensive to lose.
